title: Character Sheet — Pip locked, seeds and all
objective: Measure whether the character-sheet craftbook produces a reusable character kit: reference images covering the story's poses and expressions, a manifest that records pose, file, seed, and prompt for every reference and lists only real files, and a contact sheet with the identity written down.
prompt: we need a character sheet for Pip the dog before doing more pages — a few poses and expresions, and keep whatever you need to draw him the same later

setup.about: Comic maker project. Story notes live under workspace/story. Character kits live under workspace/characters/<name> — Pip's kit is workspace/characters/pip: reference images, the sheet.json manifest, and the sheet.html contact sheet.
setup.missionObjectives: The kit must make Pip reproducible: every reference recorded in the manifest with its seed and prompt, the palette and silhouette written down, and the manifest listing only files that really exist. No live services, no real credentials.

files.content:
# The Lighthouse Summer — story notes

Our hero: **Pip**, a small wire-haired terrier with fur the color of wet sand,
one ear permanently up and one folded down, and a mustard-yellow scarf he has
worn since page one. Short legs, big square head, brush of a tail. In shadow
you would know him by the square head and the folded ear.

Pip is brave the way small dogs are brave — first through every door, worried
about it afterwards. The pages ahead need him: sitting on the harbor wall,
running flat-out along the pier, sniffing at the lighthouse door, plus his
three faces — happy (tongue out, ear flopping), worried (ears both down, brow
knotted), and determined (leaning forward, scarf streaming).

Palette so far: sand-yellow coat, mustard scarf, storm-blue backgrounds.

success.summary: characters/pip holds 4+ references, an honest sheet.json manifest with pose/file/seed/prompt per reference, and a contact sheet carrying the palette, silhouette, and usage notes.

checks.label: every manifest file exists on disk

axes.name: consistency spec
axes.description: Silhouette, palette, and signature features are written down concretely enough that a stranger could draw Pip.

axes.name: coverage
axes.description: The references cover the poses and expressions the story notes actually call for.

axes.name: reusability
axes.description: Seeds and prompts are persisted per reference — the kit can regenerate Pip, not just remember him.

axes.name: character warmth
axes.description: The sheet reads like a beloved character's bible, not a file listing.
